text:
Alex M: Heads up — saw a sharp hit-rate collapse on the prefix cache in eu-west-1 around 09:04 UTC, hit-rate dropped ~92% -> ~4% and p99 latency spiked from 120ms -> 1.1s. Grafana: <https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/runtime?panelId=23&orgId=1|grafana>
Priya R: Yikes. Any recent deploys or config pushes? :eyes:
Mateo C: There was a small kernel-selection tweak rolled at 08:58 by CI: commit 9f3b2d. It forces AVX512 kernels for a subset of models on newer instances. Not sure why that would touch KV cache but noted.
Jin L: Also pushed a change to batching heuristics at 08:55 — aggressive batch packing for low-qps tenants to improve GPU utilization. Could increase working-set churn.
Sara P: I pulled a heap profile and kv eviction log. Lots of eviction churn starting ~09:03. Example:
```
[09:03:12] eviction reason=size prefix=tenant:acct_42:conv:len=512 added_size=4096
[09:03:12] evicting shard=14 keys=128 -> new_used=98MB
[09:03:13] prefix_cache.hit_rate=0.042
```
Alex M: ops-bot shows a config roll earlier by infra: `REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE_MAX=20000 -> 4000` at 08:59. Link: <https://deploy.internal/r/789|deploy>
Mateo C: That param change would explain sudden shrink of capacity. If we reduced max entries 5x and tenant working sets are larger due to batching request patterns, eviction wave is expected.
Priya R: Who owns that config change? We need immediate mitigation if it's a production SLA issue.
ops-bot: @here deploy infra/config rollback completed by infra-bot at 09:05, job id 789-rollback. Status: success :white_check_mark:
Jin L: Confirmed rollback finished at 09:05:12. Hit-rate recovered partially to ~60% by 09:08 but still below baseline.
Sara P: Partial recovery likely because hot prefixes were already evicted and need to be repopulated. Warmup depends on traffic — we can prime top prefixes by replaying recent requests to KV or let live traffic warm them.
Alex M: Can we identify noisy tenants that caused eviction? Logs show lots of long prefixes from `acct_42` and `acct_108` — both had bursts of numerous low-value prefixes (length 512-2048).
Mateo C: That smells like prefix-key poisoning — a tenant sending many unique prefixes to thrash the shared cache. We should add per-tenant admission controls.
Priya R: Short-term: 1) increase per-node prefix cache memory cap back to baseline (done via rollback). 2) throttle per-tenant prefix inserts (rate-limit new prefix keys). 3) mark tenants for mitigation and contact support.
Jin L: I pushed a quick defensive guard in staging earlier: reject insert if prefix_len > 1024 or inserts/sec per tenant > 200. Snippet:
```
if (prefix.size() > 1024 || tenant.insert_rate() > 200) {
  drop_insert(); // protect cache
}
```
Sara P: Need to be careful with hard limits — some enterprise customers legitimately have long prefix chains. Use RL with alerting instead of blackhole.
Alex M: Agreed. For now we enabled per-tenant insert throttling at the proxy layer for the top offenders only (acct_42, acct_108). Latency is trending down: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms.
Mateo C: We should also correlate kernel-selection change — I'm going to run a microbenchmark across both kernel variants; maybe AVX512 path has different memory access pattern affecting eviction timing.
Jin L: I'll rollback batching heuristic in eu-west-1 to previous soft packing policy and watch if working-set locality improves.
Priya R: Action items:
- Mateo: perf microbench on kernel variants + report in #eng-runtime (ETA 2h)
- Jin: revert batching heuristic in region (done, observing) (ETA 30m)
- Sara: prepare warmup job to reseed hot prefixes (ETA 15m)
- Alex: notify CS for acct_42/108 and open follow-up ticket for per-tenant shaping

Mateo C: Quick note — profiler shows higher allocator churn during the eviction wave; might be exacerbated by our slab allocator fallback when many small prefixes are created.
Sara P: Good catch. Add slab metrics to dashboards and trigger alert when alloc churn > 10k/s.
Alex M: Thanks all. I'll keep monitoring. If hit-rate hits baseline (>85%) and latency stable, we'll close thread. :thumbsup:
Priya R: Thanks — postmortem and follow-ups please (assign owner for long-term fixes).
